name: Selena
summary: Selena is an R&D programme for a large selenium imaging detector combining neutrinoless double-beta-decay searches with solar-neutrino spectroscopy. Small imaging sensors have been tested; the proposed tonne-scale detector is not built.
detection_principle: An amorphous selenium ionization layer is deposited on a CMOS active-pixel sensor. Fine tracks and spatially correlated radioactive daughters provide event identification for selenium-82 decays and neutrino capture.

science_scope: A neutrinoless decay would violate lepton number. Half-life sensitivity is a forecast unless explicitly reported as an experimental limit; its interpretation as an effective Majorana mass depends on the decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements.
